← Model Evals

Review progress

983 / 2890 model–benchmark pairs reviewed across 124 models.

Each comparison belongs to one publisher report. Benchmark-maintainer evaluations are reviewed separately for the exact version, subset and metric. “Not yet reviewed” does not mean a result is unavailable. Source verification checks transcription and evaluation scope; it does not reproduce the experiment.

Reviewed includes documented unresolved sources and incompatible setups; these never enter the official ranking. Partial source comparisons stay in progress even when the leaderboard review is done. Models are complete only after source coverage and every collected metric have been reviewed. 1135 catalog-only identities have no collected results and are not counted as reviewed.

October 24 Kimi audit and complete official snapshots ↗

Figure 8.12.1.A, PDF p.190 · published 2026-09-22 · checked 2026-10-26

Source-specific conditions retained per row; supplementary evidence does not replace the headline.

Latency is derived from fixed reference prefill/decode rates plus measured tool time, with hand-off clocks; it is not raw serving wall time. ProgramBench uses the longest agent trajectory; DRACO uses the lead’s final clock. Tokens count each input/output token once per context window and are summed across agents. No score, token or latency coordinates are estimated. The prose reports 2.7× latency improvement for five agents at score 0.6; that is a conditional speedup, not a terminal score. Fixed peers have no lead; each has a separate checkout and the run ends when all agents finish.

Figure 8.12.2.A, PDF p.192 · published 2026-09-22 · checked 2026-10-26

Source-specific conditions retained per row; supplementary evidence does not replace the headline.

Latency is derived from fixed reference prefill/decode rates plus measured tool time, with hand-off clocks; it is not raw serving wall time. ProgramBench uses the longest agent trajectory; DRACO uses the lead’s final clock. Tokens count each input/output token once per context window and are summed across agents. Budgets scale each task’s single-agent latency. The prose describes roughly 2.8× speedup for the five-agent 0.5× budget; no exact score follows from it. A fixed-team lead ends the DRACO run; all share one filesystem. Async agents see the lead’s instructions, not the original task; there is no subagent count cap.
